name: Ginat
title: Father of Tibni
summary: Ginat is known from the Bible solely as the father of Tibni, who competed with Omri for royal power in the northern kingdom of Israel after King Elah's death. Ginat himself played no direct role in the biblical accounts, but his son Tibni was supported by a portion of the people in the ensuing struggle for power.

keyEvents.title: Tibni's Struggle for the Throne
keyEvents.description: After Zimri committed suicide, the people of Israel were divided into two factions. Half followed Tibni, son of Ginat, while the other half followed Omri.

keyEvents.title: Omri Defeats Tibni
keyEvents.description: Omri's supporters overcame Tibni, son of Ginat. Tibni died, and Omri became sole king over Israel.

keyEvents.title: Context: The Death of Elah and Zimri's Coup
keyEvents.description: King Elah, son of Baasha, was killed by his servant Zimri, who seized power in Tirzah. This created the chaos that led to the civil war in which Tibni, son of Ginat, was involved.

keyEvents.title: Omri Becomes King over All Israel
keyEvents.description: After Tibni's death, Omri became the sole king of Israel and founded a new dynasty. Gibbethon is thus indirectly mentioned in connection with this important shift of power.
